title: Polynomial local factorizations of Koszul lci scheme morphisms
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume that every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood on which $f$ factors as a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], with the closed immersion ideal locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. For every $x\in X$ and every open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ containing $f(x)$ [def-weil-open-immersion], there exist an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ of $x$, an integer $n\geq0$, and an immersion $a:U\to\mathbf A^n_V$ over $V$ [def-sbc-affine-space] such that $f|_U$ is the composite of $a$ and the projection to $V$, followed by $V\hookrightarrow Y$. The immersion $a$ is Koszul-regular: locally it is a closed immersion into an open subscheme of $\mathbf A^n_V$ whose ideal is locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence. No Noetherian, flatness, separation, or quasi-compactness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 069E (lemma-koszul-independence-factorization), 069F (definition-lci) and the paragraphs immediately before and after it, and 069G (lemma-lci). The target-open refinement is the same local factorization applied over V.

proof.text: Fix $x$ and $V$. Choose the assumed factorization $X_0\xrightarrow{j}P\xrightarrow{p}Y$, with $x\in X_0$, $j$ a Koszul-regular closed immersion and $p$ smooth. Choose an affine open $T=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset V$ containing $f(x)$ and an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset p^{-1}(T)$ containing $j(x)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a) the restriction $W\to T$ of $p$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; it is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the ring map $A\to B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (transport along the isomorphisms $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$, $T\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ by part (c)), so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] makes $A\to B$ a smooth ring map, in particular finitely presented. Finite presentation means a presentation $B=A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. By the affine description of closed immersions in [def-weil-closed-immersion], $Z=j^{-1}(W)=\operatorname{Spec}(B/I)$ for an ideal $I\subset B$. This is an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $X_0$, lies in $f^{-1}(V)$, and $Z\hookrightarrow W$ is still Koszul-regular. Indeed, let $z\in Z$, and let $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset P$ be an affine open containing $j(z)$ on which the ideal of $j$ is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Choose $g\in R$ with $j(z)\in D(g)\subset W\cap\operatorname{Spec}R$. On $D(g)=\operatorname{Spec}R_g$ the ideal is generated by the $f_k/1$, and $K_\bullet(f_1/1,\ldots,f_r/1)=K_\bullet(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\otimes_RR_g$ has $H_i=H_i(K_\bullet(f_1,\ldots,f_r))_g=0$ for $i\neq0$, because localization is exact. These opens $D(g)$ cover $j(Z)$ inside $W$.

source.place: Tag 069F, preceding polynomial factorization remark; use the supplied smooth factorization and affine-local smoothness.

proof.text: Compose the surjections $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B\twoheadrightarrow B/I$. The resulting surjection defines a closed immersion $b:Z\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}(A[t_1,\ldots,t_n])=\mathbf A^n_T$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-affine-space]. It is over $T$: both composites to $T$ are induced by the same constants map $A\to B/I$, and the contravariant functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ in [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identifies the composite with $f|_Z$ viewed over $T$. No regularity assertion about the kernel of this polynomial presentation has yet been used.

source.place: Tag 069F, preceding polynomial factorization remark (affine case of Tag 04II, morphisms.tex lemma-quasi-affine-finite-type-over-S).

proof.text: Write $\beta_i\in B$ for the images of the presentation variables of Step 1. Put $Q=\mathbf A^n_W=\operatorname{Spec}(B[t_1,\ldots,t_n])$ using [def-sbc-affine-space]. Define $c:Z\to Q$ by the ring homomorphism which is the quotient $B\to B/I$ on constants and sends $t_i$ to $\beta_i\bmod I$. It is surjective already on constants, so $c$ is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $q:Q\to W$ be the projection and let $r:Q\to\mathbf A^n_T$ be induced by $A[t]\to B[t]$, applying $A\to B$ to coefficients and fixing each variable. The constants and variable formulas give $qc=j|_Z$ and $rc=b$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Finally $q$ is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth].

source.place: Tag 069E, graph into the product of the two smooth ambient schemes; here that product and its maps are given explicitly by polynomial algebras.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-smooth-lift] to $Z\xrightarrow{c}Q\xrightarrow{q}W$ and $j|_Z:Z\to W$. Both $c$ and $j|_Z$ are closed immersions, $q$ is smooth, $qc=j|_Z$, and $j|_Z$ is Koszul-regular by Step 1. Therefore $c$ is Koszul-regular.

The ring map $A\to B$ is smooth, so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](1), with $R'=A[t]$, makes $A[t]\to A[t]\otimes_A B$ smooth. The identification with $A[t]\to B[t]$ sends $F\otimes b$ to $bF$. Its inverse sends $\sum_\alpha b_\alpha t^\alpha$ to $\sum_\alpha t^\alpha\otimes b_\alpha$. The tensor relations check these formulas and their inverse identities termwise. So $A[t]\to B[t]$ is a smooth ring map (smoothness of ring maps is invariant under composing with a ring isomorphism, as its three defining conditions are). By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $r=\operatorname{Spec}(A[t]\to B[t])$ is smooth in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-smooth-push] to $Z\xrightarrow{c}Q\xrightarrow{r}\mathbf A^n_T$ with composite $b$. The two maps from $Z$ are closed immersions by Steps 2--3, $c$ is Koszul-regular by Step 4, and $r$ is smooth. Thus $b$ is Koszul-regular.

source.place: Tag 0693, lemma-push-regular-immersion-thru-smooth; smoothness of r uses algebra.tex base-change-smooth, the polynomial form of morphisms.tex 01VB.

proof.text: Set $U=Z$. By [def-sbc-affine-space], $\mathbf A^n_T$ is the inverse image of the open $T\subset V$ under $\mathbf A^n_V\to V$. Thus $\mathbf A^n_T\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_V$ is an open immersion: its structure sheaf is the restriction to that open subset, as in [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $a$ be $b$ followed by this open inclusion. It is a closed immersion into the open $\mathbf A^n_T$ and therefore an immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its local ideals there are exactly those for $b$, Koszul-regular by Step 5. The constants-map identity in Step 2 followed by $T\hookrightarrow V\hookrightarrow Y$ gives the required factorization. All choices were neighbourhoods of $x$, with $U\subset f^{-1}(V)$; no global finiteness or separation condition was used.
